image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a grey whale breaching or surfacing in the ocean. The head and anterior body are visible above the water line, showing characteristic mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches. Water droplets are spraying from the snout area. The background consists of calm blue ocean water and a pale sky.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey coloration with distinct white/cream-colored patches consistent with barnacle clusters on the rostrum and head.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or obscured by water/spray. Baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are located on the underside/lateral aspect further back than the visible frame allows. They are completely occluded by the water or out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is entirely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution detail on the snout and head shows the rough, uneven texture typical of callosities and barnacle encrustations.

The boundary where the whale's skin meets the water surface has a slight softness/halo effect, lacking the crisp refraction expected in a high-speed photograph.

The very tip of the snout appears slightly rounded and soft, potentially lacking the precise anatomical definition of a real grey whale's rostrum, though this could also be due to motion blur simulation.
